summary: Set keeps unique values and iterates in insertion order.
documentation: Set keeps unique values and iterates in insertion order. For strings it distinguishes case; repeated occurrences do not create extra entries. Objects are compared by identity, not by their field contents.
caution: Convert a Set to an array before returning JSON. Object deduplication needs an explicit key policy if equal-looking objects should count as duplicates.
scenarios: Combine tag lists while retaining the first-seen order.
Remove repeated staff identifiers from a local selection.
Track unique category names encountered during an import.
title: Merge unique tag lists
problem: Input has first and second arrays of strings. Return a single array of unique tags, scanning first before second. Preserve first occurrence order, case and empty strings.
goal: Use Set or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Concatenate both lists, construct a Set, then materialize an array.
